He first points to the engine bay, then steps back to explain the car's features while gesturing. The segment concludes with a close-up of him plugging a charging cable into the vehicle's front charging port, highlighting its electric nature.

At an automotive exhibition, a representative from the Korea Environment Corporation, Yoo Dong-kun, is interviewed while standing beside a light blue electric vehicle plugged into a charging station. He discusses the corporation's initiative to establish a charging infrastructure, noting that they previously built a system to support up to 500 electric vehicles and are now planning to build another. The scene highlights the promotion and development of electric vehicle technology in Korea.

A representative from the Korea Environment Corporation, Yoo, Dong-kun, is interviewed in a news segment about electric vehicle infrastructure. He speaks in front of a display of informational panels and a charging station, explaining that the current charging infrastructure has a capacity for 2,600 vehicles and that expanding this network will encourage more electric car adoption, leading to reduced carbon emissions and improved air quality.

A representative from the Korea Environment Corporation, Yoo, Dong-kun, is interviewed at a trade show, discussing environmental technology. The scene cuts to a display of his company's equipment, including sensors and a monitor showing real-time data, highlighting their role in reducing carbon emissions and improving air quality.

At a trade show booth, a presenter demonstrates a sophisticated real-time monitoring system. They hold a small sensor in one hand and a metallic tuning fork in the other, using them to interact with the system. The large monitor displays multiple live data streams—including pressure, voltage, current, and graphs—indicating the system is actively measuring and recording the physical properties of the sensor and tuning fork as they are manipulated.

A person demonstrates advanced sensor technology at a trade show, using a computer monitor displaying real-time data graphs—including a prominent FFT strain analysis—and handling various sensors, such as a fork-shaped accelerometer and pressure transducers, to showcase their capabilities for industrial monitoring and diagnostics.
